# Board Brief: Synthetic pump fire, 2024

*Learning purposes: not a statutory document*

**Audience:** Board and its safety committee

**Incident:** Synthetic pump fire · 2024-03-20

## Bottom line

- Seals were bought without a specification for two years before the fire. [FND-0003; EVD-0003]
- No check stopped an untested pump returning to service. [FND-0002]

## What happened and why it matters to the board

A pump was restarted after a seal change without a leak test and the seal failed [FND-0001; EVD-0001].

## What the investigation says about the management system

Spares were bought locally without a specification, and assurance did not see the gap [FND-0003].

## Questions for directors to ask management

**Q: How do we know critical spares meet their specification at every site?** [FND-0003]
- Why it matters: Local purchasing bypassed the specification for two years.
- Good evidence looks like: A sampled audit of critical-spares purchase records against specifications.
- Put to: Chief Executive

**Q: Which equipment can return to service without a documented test?** [FND-0002]
- Why it matters: The pump restarted without one.
- Good evidence looks like: A list of return-to-service hold points with test records.

## Assurance the board should request

| Verification | Sites | By when | Cites |
|---|---|---|---|
| Independent check of critical-spares specifications | All sites | Next quarter | FND-0003 |

## Indicators for the board dashboard

**Indicator:** Critical spares bought to specification [FND-0003]
- Measure: % of critical-spares orders with a specification reference
- Deterioration looks like: Any month below 100%
- Owner: Head of procurement
